summary: The change removes the origin allow-list and unconditionally returns both `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (reflecting the caller or `*`) and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. This combination is a security violation: credentialed requests from arbitrary origins become possible. The prior explicit allow-list was the only protection; nothing else in the codebase constrains callers.

verification.reason: Head `corsHeaders` always sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to the request origin (or `*`) together with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, removing the previous allowlist. That is the classic credentials+reflected-origin CORS misconfiguration and a real security regression.
